resources.string: Exact answers to everyday sums: fuel, battery, currency and more. No model needed.
I have 23 L of water and 5 L jerrycans. How many jerrycans do I need?
How long to drive 240 miles at 60 mph?
Exact answers to everyday sums, with the formula. No model needed.
My power bank is 5,000 mAh at 3.85 V. Can I take it on a plane?
5,000 mAh × 3.85 V ÷ 1000 = 19.25 Wh. Yes, you can take it on a plane: up to 100 Wh is allowed in carry-on baggage (not in checked bags).

It works out the answer from the numbers in your question and shows the formula. It knows: a battery\'s watt-hours and whether it can fly; fuel economy (L/100 km, mpg); hiking time (Naismith\'s rule); currency at your rate, with a tip; water for a trip; Celsius and Fahrenheit; how long at a rate; how many containers, trips or buses, rounded up.\n\nPlain sums and percentages still go to the model. Calculator stays out of conversations about health, injuries, danger or people, and goes to the model instead. The answer\'s details say Tool when it wrote it. Word problems (how long, how many) are English only. Based on r4to\'s calculator (BOAR R&D).
